steps.title: Using price comparison sites
steps.body: Sites like Tweakers Pricewatch or Google Shopping show in one overview where a product is cheapest, including shipping costs and the shop's rating.

steps.title: Checking discount codes
steps.body: Before checking out: search '[shop name] discount code' or check a student-discount app. There's often a valid code for free shipping or a percentage off.

steps.title: Checking price history
steps.body: Some tools (like the Camelizer browser extension) show whether a 'deal' you saw in an Instagram or TikTok ad is a real deal, or whether the price was just as low a few weeks ago.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Compare the price of a product you're interested in at two different web shops.

lessons.title: Paying without worries (and without building up debt)

steps.title: iDEAL and credit card
steps.body: At well-known Dutch web shops you usually pay safely with iDEAL (via your own bank) or credit card. Both offer protection if something goes wrong with your order.

steps.title: Buy now, pay later: the trap that catches a lot of young people
steps.body: Services like Klarna or Riverty let you 'buy now, pay later'. Handy, but it also makes impulse buying too easy — and miss a payment deadline and collection fees can pile up fast, along with a negative credit record that can follow you for years. Always set a reminder for the payment date, and don't treat it as 'free money'.

steps.title: Subscription traps
steps.body: A 'free trial' that automatically turns into a paid subscription after a month is a well-known pitfall. Read the fine print and, if needed, set a reminder right away to cancel on time.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: With a 'buy now, pay later' option, check exactly when the payment deadline falls.

steps.title: Checking track & trace quickly
steps.body: Most delivery services have an app (PostNL, DHL) that lets you track all your parcels in one overview, instead of looking up separate track & trace links.

steps.title: Comparing return policies
steps.body: Not every shop uses the same deadline. Check this before buying, especially for clothing or electronics: some shops offer 30 or even 100 days to change your mind — handy if something doesn't fit or you change your mind.

steps.title: Knowing your legal warranty rights
steps.body: Besides the warranty a shop offers itself, you always have a right to legal warranty for a faulty product — it simply has to do what you can reasonably expect, regardless of what the shop says about it.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Look up the return policy of a web shop you order from often.

lessons.title: Spotting fake web shops and review fraud (including ones from social media ads)

steps.title: Spotting a fake web shop quickly
steps.body: Watch for: a very new domain, no company registration number, only a contact form with no phone number, and prices that are too good to be true. Check the domain on a tool like whois.com for its registration date — fake shops that show up via an Instagram or TikTok ad are often only a few weeks old.

steps.title: Recognizing review fraud
steps.body: Many identical reviews around the same date, only 5 stars with no text, or reviews using the exact same phrases — all signs of bought or fake reviews.

steps.title: Payment method as a warning sign
steps.body: Is only an upfront bank transfer accepted, with no iDEAL, credit card, or PayPal option? With a scam you can almost never get that transfer back — a big reason to walk away, however tempting the 'deal' looks.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Think about it: which three signs would help you spot a fake web shop the fastest?
